newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian banks must boost competitiveness - Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Italian banks must boost competitiveness - Fazio.

text.p: Italian central bank governor Antonio Fazio said in an interview Italian banks needed to reduce costs and become more efficient in offering services in order to remain competitive with foreign banks.
Fazio, in an interview with Euromoney magazine, said generally the Italian banking system was reasonably well established and efficient in more traditional markets.

"But Italy's banks will have to reduce costs, especially labour costs, and become more innovative and efficient in the supply of services in order to remain competitive with foreign banks and other intermediaries," he said.
The interview was released by the Bank of Italy ahead of publication on Wednesday.
"The supply of long-term finance is still insufficiently developed," he said.

Fazio also rejected the idea competition and consolidation in banking were divergent goals, saying that to achieve them banks must "work actively to reduce costs, increase efficiency and enhance the quality" of products and services.
The interview was carried out in August. Euromoney has named Fazio its central banker of the Year.
